I'm sitting here thinking about this year like I always do — what did I do last year, and should I change anything. My 16.1 mu is split up: I put wheat and maize on the same 10 mu, rotating them like I've done for 30 years. Cotton takes another 4 mu on the sandier piece near the road. Garlic goes on 2.1 mu — the plot closest to the well because garlic drinks a lot of water.

For wheat, I plant an improved variety the agro-shop sells — Jimai type, same as my neighbors. I put about two bags of compound fertilizer (40kg bags, 15-15-15) before plowing, then top-dress with one bag of urea (50kg) when I irrigate in spring around Qingming. That comes to roughly 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg phosphate, 6 kg potash. I irrigate 3 times — winter water, spring green-up, and grain-filling. Spray twice for aphids and rust. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu, I'll aim the same.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed — everyone does, the old varieties don't yield. One bag compound before planting, then topdress urea at big flare stage. Around 18 kg N, 6 P, 5 K per mu. Irrigate twice if rain is poor. Spray once for borer, once for armyworm if I see them. Expect 550 kg per mu.

Cotton is more trouble. I use improved Bt cotton seed so I don't spray so much for bollworm. Still need 4-5 sprays for aphids and spider mites. Put two bags compound before planting, topdress urea at budding and flowering. About 18 kg N, 8 P, 8 K per mu. Irrigate 3 times. Get maybe 250 kg seed cotton per mu.

Garlic needs heavy feeding — it's my cash crop. I put plenty of manure from my neighbor's chicken shed plus two bags compound, then topdress twice with urea. Around 25 kg N, 12 P, 10 K per mu. Irrigate 5 times, it doesn't like dry. Spray twice for leaf blight. Last year got 1800 kg per mu and the price was decent.

Rotary till everything — I rent the tractor from the village, plowing deep every 3 years only. I don't change much from year to year. What worked before works again.
